Include an atmospheric academy hall or study scene, a student profile with rank and progress, a curriculum of magical course cards, a prominent current lesson, an upcoming exam panel, spell mastery indicators, and one clear Learn or Practice action. Put strong emphasis on an enchanting scholarly identity, readable progression, meaningful card differentiation, elegant typography, and polished visual craft.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The single largest gap is the missing 'curriculum of magical course cards' — the left column is a stack of stat tiles (Spellcraft Hours, Perfect Exams, Day Streak, Arcane Hours), not course cards, so 'meaningful card differentiation' is unfulfilled and the only card-like content is one lesson plus the exam. The required 'one clear Learn or Practice action' is also absent: the current lesson card shows '22 min left' and '+120 XP' but no Continue/Practice button, while the only filled CTA on screen is the exam panel's 'Review Weak Topics', which misdirects the primary action toward exam prep instead of learning. The atmospheric hall is present but reads as a mid-size banner of flat gray trapezoid arches rather than a lived-in academy scene. Clarity & Hierarchy: Focal priority is split four ways (63% ring, scene, exam countdown, lesson title); the brief's 'prominent current lesson' is buried below the scene and lacks a CTA. Progression is triple-encoded and inconsistent — profile says 320/500 XP (64%), the ring says 63%, and a third bar says '180 XP to Rank IV' — three competing signals for one fact. The 'THE GRAND HALL' label collides with the glowing orb, and the Spell Mastery panel is clipped at the fold, implying the curriculum (if it exists) is off-screen. Visual System & Craft: Palette is coherent but progress-bar hues (gold/pink/blue) lack a stated semantic; the corner-bracket motif is applied to some panels (rank, exam, mastery) but not the lesson or scene, breaking the system; the scene's arches are low-detail and flat against the otherwise refined gold-on-indigo craft; header elements (logo, wordmark, floating date pill, profile) sit on uneven baselines. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The scholarly voice is genuinely strong ('The Athenaeum', 'Est. 1247', 'rites', 'Proving of Elements', sigil), but distinctiveness currently lives almost entirely in copy — the visual cards are near-identical dark panels, and the one atmospheric moment (the hall) is underdeveloped, so the page risks reading as a generic dark dashboard with fantasy labels.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan that keeps all required content: (1) Add the missing curriculum — insert a 'Curriculum' row of 3–4 course cards directly under the scene, each meaningfully differentiated by state and identity: e.g. Alchemy (In Progress, blue accent, 4/7 rites), Runes (Available, gold accent, 'Begin'), Divination (Locked, dimmed, 'Requires Rank IV'), each with its own sigil icon, mastery pips, and next-rite label. To fund this space, compress the four left stat tiles into a single slim horizontal strip and shorten the scene to a wide hero band — the explicit trade-off is scene height for curriculum visibility, which the brief favors. (2) Create the single primary action: give the current lesson card a filled gold 'Continue Rite · 4 of 7' button as the only solid CTA on the page, and demote 'Review Weak Topics' to a ghost/text link; this resolves the competing-CTA trade-off in favor of the brief's Learn/Practice emphasis and makes the lesson the clear focal point (brighter border, slightly larger, directly beneath the scene). (3) Unify progression to one source of truth: keep 320/500 XP in the profile, set the left ring to the same 64% (fixing the 63% mismatch), label its bar '180 XP to Rank IV', and remove the duplicate 'Rank III' text so rank is read in one place. (4) Deepen the scene for atmosphere without new assets: layer the arches with vertical gradients, add a floor reflection under the orb, floating dust motes, and faint bookshelf/candle silhouettes plus a vignette, and move 'THE GRAND HALL' into a clean caption chip so it no longer overlaps the orb. (5) Systematize craft: assign fixed color semantics (gold = rank/XP, blue = active lesson, magenta = exam, green = positive deltas), apply the corner-bracket motif consistently to every panel card, and reflow the right column so Exam and Spell Mastery share a 2-up grid that fits above the fold (no clipping). (6) Typography pass: align logo/wordmark/date/profile on one baseline grid, reserve the italic-gold treatment for the wordmark and key numerals only, and tighten label letter-spacing. Sequence the work as 1 → 2 → 3 first (they fix the brief's omissions and hierarchy), then 4 → 5 → 6 for craft and expression.

The exam's three rose bars read as one metric family, and 'Mock exam score 82' rendered as a bar is ambiguous. The blue lesson bar and the blue 'Primal Elements' title text clash with the gold/rose/indigo system. The scene contains stray unfilled rectangle outlines that read as unfinished placeholders, and the spotlight beams are flat trapezoids. Card treatment is uneven: corner-bracket ticks appear on three cards but not the lesson or scene. The lesson title breaks awkwardly across two lines. (6) De-duplicate progression: keep the ring as the single rank truth, reduce the profile card to name/rank + a thin bar, remove or merge the separate 'TO RANK IV' bar, and rename the confusing 'Streak' stat. (7) Type polish: set the lesson title in one display treatment with a single gold italic accent word and fix the awkward line break. Order matters: 1–3 fix brief and overflow first, 4–5 strengthen craft and expression, 6–7 are final polish.
